Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 86, verses 1–4:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-Tariq (the Night-Comer), because it opens with Allah's oath by "the sky and the al-Tariq," which is the bright star that appears at night.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Affirming and emphasizing that every person has been assigned an angel who guards him and records his deeds, and refuting what the polytheists considered impossible regarding resurrection, by presenting evidence of Allah's power to restore a human being after his death. Implicit in this is a reminder of the precision of Allah's creation and His wisdom in creating man.

• Extolling the status of the Qur'an, and implicitly indicating the truthfulness of what it says about resurrection, warning the polytheists who opposed the Muslims, affirming the Prophet (ﷺ), and promising him that Allah will soon grant him victory.

[Tafsir]

Allah, glorified is He, swears by the sky and the star that appears at night. And what will make you know what the greatness of this star is? It is the bright, blazing star. There is no soul but that an angel, a watchful guardian, has been appointed over it to preserve its deeds, so that it may be called to account for them on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 86, verses 5–8:

So let the human being who denies the resurrection look at what he was created from. Let him know that re-creating the human being is not harder than creating him at first. He was created from a fluid (maniyy) poured forth swiftly into the womb, which emerges from between the backbone of the man and the chest of the woman. Indeed, the One who created the human being from this water is certainly able to return him to life after death.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 86, verses 11–14:

By the sky with its recurring rain, and the earth with its splitting open to bring forth what grows from it. Indeed, the Qur'an is a decisive word that distinguishes truth from falsehood, and it is not a matter of jest. It is not permissible for a created being to swear by other than Allah, and whoever does so has committed shirk.

The Noble Qur'an, with the Explanation of Al-Tafsir Al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex)

On surah 86, verses 15–17:

Indeed, those who deny the Messenger ﷺ and the Qur'an are plotting and scheming, so that by their scheming they may repel the truth and support falsehood. But I (Allah) am plotting a plot to make the truth manifest, even though the disbelievers dislike it. So do not hasten on their behalf, O Messenger, by seeking the sending down of punishment upon them. Rather, give them respite and delay them a little, and do not hasten for them; you will see what befalls them of torment, retribution, punishment, and destruction.
